pattern_title: OH LTSS Dual Eligible SNF spend jumped on both volume and rate
pattern_description: Ohio free-standing SNF spend for LTSS Dual Eligible members rose sharply across both authorization statuses. Most of the increase came from non-PA claims, but the PA-required slice also showed more admissions and higher paid per admit. This is a combined utilization and reimbursement issue in one facility type, not just a broad Medicaid trend.

claims.summary: OH LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF spend increased by +$50.3M across PA-required and non-PA claims. The non-PA slice drove +$40.1M with 5,772 more admissions and about +$6,949 paid per admit. The PA-required slice added +$10.2M with 977 more admissions and about +$10,462 paid per admit.

pattern_title: OH TANF Standard SNF growth is blurred by a large Not Mapped bucket
pattern_description: Ohio TANF Standard costs rose through two different mechanisms: a large SNF volume increase in non-PA claims and a separate authorized bucket recorded as Not Mapped with very high paid per admit. Because a material share of the increase sits in an unmapped facility category, facility classification needs to be corrected before broad site-of-care or pricing action. After validation, the remaining SNF growth should be managed through admission and level-of-care controls.

claims.summary: OH TANF Standard spend increased by +$19.1M across SNF and Not Mapped facility classifications. The Not Mapped authorized bucket added +$10.1M with 408 more admissions and about +$21.6K paid per admit. The non-PA free-standing SNF bucket added +$9.1M with 1,314 more admissions while paid per admit was nearly flat.

pattern_title: Authorization-code shifts are creating false cost signals in CA, IN, and TN
pattern_description: Several states show material movement in authorization-code assignment rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement story. California, Indiana, and Tennessee each have sizable cost change tied to authorization-code distribution, including provider-specific concentration at Riley's Children's Health, Fresno Heart & Surgical Hospital, and Methodist University Hospital. These records should be reconciled before tightening PA policy, changing reimbursement, or escalating provider action.

pattern_title: Behavioral health admissions and acuity are rising across NC, GA, VA, NY, IA, and WV
pattern_description: Behavioral health is a recurring cost theme across multiple states, with both inpatient behavioral health and acute psych facility growth. North Carolina and Virginia are led by depressive, stress, and adjustment-related admissions, while Georgia is concentrated at RIDGEVIEW INSTITUTE MONROE across both acute psych products and inpatient behavioral health. Smaller acute psych increases in New York, Iowa, and West Virginia show the same pattern of rising admissions with added unit-cost pressure.

pattern_title: CA inpatient Med/Surg mix is shifting toward transplant, liver disease, and other rare high-cost cases
pattern_description: California inpatient Med/Surg spend reflects a focused case-mix shift toward liver disease, kidney transplant complications, and a smaller set of rare high-cost admissions. The recurring liver and kidney cases suggest real acuity pressure, while bariatric surgery, transplant-related complications, and low-baseline nursing-facility cases should be validated before broad policy changes. This should be handled as a targeted clinical and validation workstream, not a general statewide inpatient rate issue.
